lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: It's the old proverb exactly! The fawn catches the lion.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: What are you so upset about, Cnemon?

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: You ask what I'm upset about? I've been completely outplayed, idiot that I am. I've left my estate to an heir I didn't want, and entirely cut out the people I actually wanted to have it.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: I was courting Hermolaus for his legacy—he's incredibly rich, no children—and he was perfectly happy to soak up the attention. Then I had what I thought was a stroke of genius: I drew up my will in public, leaving him absolutely everything, assuming he'd take the hint and do exactly the same for me.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: What he put in his will, I haven't the faintest idea. The roof collapsed on me and I died instantly! Now Hermolaus has everything I own. Like a greedy sea bass, he swallowed the hook right along with the bait.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Not just the hook—he dragged in the fisherman, too! [laughs] You really set that trap perfectly for yourself.
